html: The Yaquina were a Native people of Yaquina Bay and the Yaquina River on the central Oregon coast, around present Newport. They spoke a dialect of the Alsea language, shared with the Alsea to the south. They lived in villages of plank houses, fishing, gathering shellfish and trading along the coast. In 1855 their land became part of the Coast Reservation; much of it was soon opened to settlers, and the remaining Yaquina joined the Siletz reservation. Their language died out in the 1900s. To the north lived the Siletz Tillamook.
